hero.title: Wake up in a Pueblo Mágico.
hero.subtitle: A boutique hostel for travelers who want more than a bed — mezcal nights, mountain mornings, and the kind of people you tell stories about for years.

king-suite.name: Private King Suite
king-suite.short: Stone walls, king bed, private terrace facing the Tepozteco.
long: The King Suite is Casa Xicun's quietest room — a private corner at the top of the property, where the only sound at night is wind moving through the pines.
A locally carved king bed sits under exposed beams. Stone walls hold the cool. A private terrace catches the morning light over the mountain.
Built for couples, anniversaries, and travelers who came to slow down.

boho-double.name: Boho Double
boho-double.short: Bright queen room with handwoven textiles and a mountain peek.
long: The Boho Double is our most-photographed room — bright walls, handwoven textiles from the Saturday market, a queen bed with linen sheets.
Mountain peek from the window, a writing desk for slow mornings, and an en-suite with stone shower.
For solo travelers who want their own door, and friends sharing a queen.

social-dorm.name: Social Dorm (4 beds)
social-dorm.short: Custom-built bunks, blackout curtains, lockers, shared rooftop access.
long: Not your average hostel dorm. Four custom-built bunks, each with a curtain, reading light, USB ports, and a deep locker.
Linen sheets, blackout curtains, climate control. Shared bathroom kept hotel-clean.
Mixed-gender by default. Solo travelers, digital nomads, and anyone who'd rather meet people than stare at hotel wallpaper.

garden-double.name: Garden Double
garden-double.short: Ground-floor double opening onto the courtyard garden.
long: Garden Double opens straight onto our walled courtyard — fig trees, bougainvillea, the sound of the morning coffee being poured.
Queen bed, soft cream linens, an en-suite with a copper sink and stone floor.
For travelers who want to step out of bed into the green.

house.title: A small house with a long story.
house.intro: Casa Xicun is an old Tepozteco family home, restored room by room over three years. The bones are 19th-century stone; everything you touch was made by someone we know.

story.heading: The build
story.body: We worked with local masons, carpenters from Amatlán, and a third-generation tile maker from Cuentepec. Nothing was shipped from a catalog.

story.heading: The land
story.body: Walking distance to the market, the mezcalerías, and the trailhead. Fifteen minutes by car to Tepozteco's base camp.

story.heading: Wedding & group stays
story.body: We host one wedding party a month — full buyout, late check-out, a cooked breakfast for everyone. Ask us.
